title: Is the office Christmas party worth defending?

turns.speaker: Brendan
turns.text: They've replaced the party with a voucher. Forty pounds each and no evening.

turns.speaker: Ola
turns.text: Most people I know would take the voucher without hesitating.

turns.speaker: Fay
turns.text: Which tells you what the party was actually worth to them, doesn't it.

turns.speaker: Brendan
turns.text: It tells you what it was worth compared to forty pounds, which isn't quite the same thing.

turns.speaker: Ola
turns.text: The case for it is the weak ties. You end up talking to someone from a floor you never visit, and six months later that's who you ask for a favour.

turns.speaker: Fay
turns.text: That's real and it's also the bit an evening of enforced drinking does badly.

turns.speaker: Fay
turns.text: If you don't drink, or you've got childcare at six, you're excluded from the thing that's supposed to include you.

turns.speaker: Brendan
turns.text: Which describes a fairly large share of any workforce.

turns.speaker: Ola
turns.text: So a lunch instead. Same mixing, inside working hours, nobody has to arrange anything.

turns.speaker: Brendan
turns.text: Less fun, though. I'd rather be honest that something is being traded.

turns.speaker: Fay
turns.text: Fun for the people the evening was already built around.

turns.speaker: Ola
turns.text: That's fair. Although a lunch that everyone attends resentfully isn't obviously better than an evening some people love.

turns.speaker: Brendan
turns.text: The voucher avoids the whole argument, which is presumably why they chose it.

points: An office party has been replaced with a forty-pound voucher per employee.
Ola argues parties build weak ties across departments that prove useful later.
Fay counters that evening drinking events exclude non-drinkers and those with caring responsibilities, who are a large share of any workforce.
A working-hours lunch is proposed as achieving the same mixing more inclusively.
Brendan acknowledges a trade-off in enjoyment; Fay notes the enjoyment favoured those the evening was designed around.
Ola concedes a resented lunch may not be better, and Brendan observes the voucher sidesteps the argument entirely.
